#1736. Standings, highs, lows, key players: How Milan Futuro, Primavera and Women have started 2026-27

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

An ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That being said, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

It was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

Importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

High point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and currently occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

Key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the new coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games shows perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

Giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the new campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Looking upwards, Parma are currently top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

High point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

Low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around quickly.

Key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

Last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

Looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team currently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

High point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the big gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

#1735. Man City ‘doing everything we can to fix’ defensive record, says Anderson

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manchester City goalscorer Elliot Anderson says the club are "doing everything we can to fix" their defensive issues after they came from behind to draw with Fulham.

City had lost each of their last three games heading into the clash with Fulham and went behind in the 16th minute through Rodrigo Muniz's curler.

The hosts then had an Erling Haaland goal disallowed, but Anderson's first Premier League goal for City just before the hour secured all three points.

City are winless in four Premier League games (D1 L3) for the first time since January (D3 L1), while they have trailed at half-time in four consecutive matches in the competition for only the third time, after October 1995 and April 2006.

They have also conceded in nine consecutive games in all competitions for the first time since December 2019 (10), while they have conceded the opening goal in four straight Premier League outings for the first time since April 2012 (five).

Anderson acknowledged that City need to improve defensively, but he believes they are moving in the right direction.

"It's very frustrating," Anderson told BBC Sport. "Going a goal down wasn't ideal, but it seems to be happening.

"The second half was better, more intensity; we pushed higher. We just struggled to get the second goal. We're working on that [falling behind so much]. We are doing everything we can to fix it.

"I was just playing a little bit higher up – focusing on doing the best job for the team. Fighting on the ball and off the ball.

"That's my job on the edge of the box on corners from that side. Try to get a clean connection on target. Trying to stay calm in those situations and make good contact.

"Every game, we are learning things. We'll train harder. We'll be ready for the next one."

The points are shared 1-1 @okx https://t.co/X3bxDu6v8o

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 21, 2026

City almost got a quickfire equaliser, with Haaland hitting the back of the net just eight minutes after Muniz's opener.

However, Haaland's initial attempt was saved by Leno, who was then deemed to have the ball under control before the Norwegian followed in to bundle it over the line, and while Enzo Maresca did not say much when asked about the decision, he was not happy about it.

"I think it's quite clear," he told BBC Sport. "But they decided something different."

Fulham, meanwhile, are now unbeaten in their last five league games, drawing each of the last three by 1-1 scorelines.

They have now dropped 10 points from winning positions in the top-flight this season; only Brentford (11) have dropped more, but it was an impressive point for Fulham, who ended a 20-game losing streak against City in all competitions.

They defended resolutely against City's pressure, limiting them to just three shots on target out of 15 overall attempts, and Alvaro Arbeloa was impressed with the performance.

"I am happy with a point but would prefer three," he told BBC Sport. "I'm so happy with our performance – how we played and pressed them.

"We came here thinking we can beat them and not just defending. We could have scored one or two more. I'm so proud of the players."

"It wasn't easy [to persuade his players they could win against City]. After the international break, it's never easy, especially coming here.

"I told them we lost the 20 games before; we're not playing those 20 games. If we believe we can beat them. If we fight for every ball and play with character and personality, we'll have the chance to beat them. They believed and played so well."

#1733. Man City MUST stop the rot, old rivals Chelsea and Leeds set for Stamford Bridge blockbuster and Mauricio Pochettino's baptism of fire: SEVEN reasons we're excited for the return of the Premier League

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

And what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in new colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

City have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

The Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his new team currently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a new manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

However, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

They remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

But somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

The squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he said goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his new club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side currently sat in 18th

#1731. Cardinale admits Milan’s NBA Europe project could be worth €5B+: “Hottest market in Europe”

Gerry Cardinale spoke at a conference last night and it’s clear that the AC Milan owner has a lot to say on the NBA Europe matter.

The NBA Europe project has been discussed for some time now, but there has been little movement. As reports have suggested, Milan were one of the first brands/clubs to throw their hat into the ring and that interest has never died.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, it seems that some progress could be made with the plans to develop the San Donato land into an arena. However, it still feels like we are a way away from seeing an NBA team in Milano.

Speaking at the SBJ Dealmakers conference, Cardinale sat alongside the NBA Deputy Commissioner and discussed the ongoing discussions about a new European league, as MilanNews relays from Gazzetta dello Sport.

“We will continue on our path with or without an agreement because we know that in the end, we will be the ones left standing. I honestly cannot understand how we can operate for 26 years and not be able to make a profit.

“Adam Silver and Mark Tatum [who sat alongside him] are doing everything they can to reach an agreement, but it takes two people to compromise. I am convinced that in the end, the NBA will prevail.”

The American also discussed the position that Milan are in and the future of the basketball arm of the club.

“Milan is currently the hottest market in Europe. When I arrived four years ago, I had two goals, besides winning: one was the stadium, which will finally be built, and the other was to invest in basketball.

“In fact, I had conversations with Olimpia Milano well before the advent of NBA Europe. Where will NBA Europe be in 10 years? Let’s say that if the new NBA franchise in Las Vegas is valued at $13-14 billion, I think that in 10 years, NBA Europe clubs will be worth at least half that.”

#1730. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

#MUNMCI – 23'The referee's call of red card to Foden for violent conduct was checked and confirmed by VAR.REF: "Red card Phil Foden – kick out into the body of Bruno".VAR: "That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement. Confirming the red card for…

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

If you haven’t checked out the interview, you can have a read here

Fans have chanted: “You treat us like s--- Ratcliffe and the Glazers, you treat us like s---.”

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a new 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

"An absolute WORLDIE from range!"Lewis Dunk scores a contender for goal of the season 🤯 pic.twitter.com/m5bPzm5Wm3

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

There are hundreds upon hundreds of #MUFC supporters pouring through the Munich tunnel protesting against the Glazers and Ratcliffe's ownership and running of the club pic.twitter.com/VlhkMoxbmI

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

Manchester City XI: Donnarumma, Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Reis, Bouaddi, O’Reilly, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis

Your Manchester derby line-up! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Nunes, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovačić, Reis, Bouaddi, O'Reilly, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/9h5CGprFaF

It is a very offensive-minded XI with Dorgu at full-back and a midfield trio of Tielemans, Fernandes and Mainoo behind Mbeumo, Cunha and Rashford. The results could be spectacular, but City should fancy punching holes in that set up.

Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mbeumo, Cunha, Fernandes, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Heaven, Mazraoui, Yoro, Mount, Santos, Lacey, Sesko, Zirkzee.

Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1728. GdS: The ‘hero of two worlds’ – why Pulisic remains a decisive force for club and country

If anyone from AC Milan was awake to watch America’s second game against Haiti, they’d have been delighted with what they saw.

It’s been a season of confirmation for Christian Pulisic so far. He’s recently signed his renewal, confirming his long-term future with the club. More importantly, though, he’s confirmed himself as the star of Milan after a difficult first half of the year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With his current form, there’s seemingly no stopping his rise.

This morning, Gazzetta dello Sport has called him ‘the hero of two worlds’. He shone against Haiti and hopes to do the same when he returns for the Rossoneri, especially on their return to San Siro.

They haven’t yet had a chance to rectify that defeat against Ferencvaros, and this weekend’s game will give them an opportunity to do so, with Pulisic desperate to keep his fine form going.

This season alone, he’s notched up seven goals, with the latest being the bicycle kick against Haiti – which defines his form and confidence in one action.

He won’t be back in training until Friday, allowing him a day of rest. Nevertheless, he could well be given an opportunity to start by Ruben Amorim if he’s feeling ready to hit the ground running back at San Siro.

He’s back being central on all fronts again, exactly what Gerry Cardinale had hoped in the summer. Captain America is back and his new contract means he’s going nowhere.

#1726. Man United CEO Omar Berrada discusses Michael Carrick exit, Mauricio Pochettino arrival in lengthy interview

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:01

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has addressed what has been a difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign for the 20-time English champions.

The Red Devils are currently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, boasting just eight points from their opening 10 matches of the campaign.

The decision was made to sack Michael Carrick earlier this month, with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement.

Berrada has now explained the reasoning behind Carrick's dismissal and the arrival of Pochettino, who will lead Man United into Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool.

When asked whether he was confident Man United are moving in the right direction, Berrada told Sky Sports News: "One hundred per cent. I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

"It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward.

"But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction."

When asked about Carrick's dismissal, Berrada said: "It was a very difficult decision, to be honest, especially given all the affection everyone at the club has for Michael.

"When he took over the team last season, they did very well under him. They were playing some really good football, winning important matches. We qualified for the Champions League and finished third.

"We felt at the time he'd earned the right to continue leading the team. So when we started the season, it's clearly been a lot more difficult than we expected. The results haven't been good enough. I think we've dropped off in many areas.

"We wanted to give ourselves until the November international break to really take stock of what was happening with the team, what were the areas that needed to be improved. And in the end, we took the decision to make a change of coach.

"Unfortunately, sometimes when you're in the middle of the season, that's the one decision that you can make that can provoke a reaction, that can provoke a change in the dynamic. So that's why we had to take the decision."

On Pochettino, Berrada said: "He has a tremendous amount of passion and energy. We see it already in the two days he's been with us.

"There's a buzz about the place, and he's brought that with his staff. He has a very clear philosophy, identity of how he wants to see the team play. And I think he's coming just at the right time for him and us to be able to help the team and take us forward.

"He's equally as ambitious as we are, which is: we want to win titles.

"You have to think that when you're playing for Manchester United, when the results aren't going well, the pressure and the scrutiny is enormous. And all that noise around the club and around the players can be difficult to manage.

"So I think in Mauricio we bring somebody that has just the right amount of maturity and experience at the big clubs to be able to put his arms around the players and to let them perform at their highest potential."

Man United will be aiming to post just their second Premier League win of the season when they head to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon to tackle Liverpool.

#1722. Man United CEO Omar Berrada says Red Devils did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep wonderkid JJ Gabriel

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 15:09

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has insisted that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to prevent JJ Gabriel from leaving.

The 16-year-old recently posted a farewell message to Man United ahead of his expected move to Spanish giants Real Madrid.

JJ Gabriel informed Man United in September of his desire to seek pastures new, just one month before he was expected to pen scholarship terms at Old Trafford.

A professional contract was then expected to follow a year later, but JJ Gabriel's representatives informed Man United that the youngster would be looking to leave the club.

Man United have now lost a player regarded to be a generational talent, but Berrada has said that the club did "absolutely everything" in a bid to keep him.

"We did everything. Absolutely everything," Berrada told Sky Sports News when asked about JJ Gabriel's departure.

"Let's not forget with JJ, he's a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being.

"Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow.

"This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we're seeing this season with Shea Lacey.

"Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now - we're not afraid of giving young players opportunities.

"Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best. We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege."

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he has departed without making a competitive appearance for the Red Devils at first-team level.

The attacker scored 29 goals and registered four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s, in addition to two goals and two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in Premier League 2.

JJ Gabriel technically still has a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the season, but the teenager has a European passport through both of his parents, so a FIFA loophole could allow him to become a Real Madrid player from January.

Real Madrid have allegedly already mapped out a pathway for JJ Gabriel into their first team in the near future.

#1721. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1720. I can understand why fans are frustrated about lack of progress under Pocognoli, admits Andy Robertson

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026

Andy Robertson says he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no issue with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap

‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’

Having limped into the international break, Juve currently trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.

Though Juventus are on track to reach the Europa League's knockout phase without needing a playoff, domestic results have been below par for several months.

After missing out on Champions League qualification at the bitter end of last season, the Bianconeri sit seventh in Serie A and are lacking the consistency required to mount a title charge.

Remarkably, Juve have gone 10 league games without consecutively recording the same result, and they signed off for the international break with a run of one defeat, one win and one draw.

Having lost 2-0 to Genoa, before beating Napoli by the same scoreline in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's side had to fight back twice to salvage a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina last time out.

Ahead of Thursday's Europa League game and next week's clash with high-flying Como, they must avoid another slip-up when Venezia come to town.

A former coach of Sunday's visitors, Spalletti is under heavy pressure, and he will only be able to celebrate his 600th Serie A match as a manager if Juventus claim maximum points.

History suggests that the hosts should prevail, as Venezia have lost 11 of their 14 top-flight away games against Juve, while drawing the other three.

In fact, the Lagunari's last victory against the Bianconeri anywhere dates back to a home success in April 1962.

This time, they will head to Turin under survival specialist Davide Nicola, who recently replaced promotion-winning boss Giovanni Stroppa.

Though Nicola's new side impressively upset Napoli in his first match, they subsequently lost three times without scoring, ahead of a big relegation six-pointer against Udinese.

Sending Stadio Penzo into raptures, Kike Perez scored a stunning goal that separated the pair in a tense 2-1 home win for Venezia, lifting them above their hapless visitors and off the foot of the table.

However, the Arancioneroverdi have yet to pick up any points on the road, while Nicola has previously suffered seven straight defeats in his managerial head-to-head with Spalletti.

Though Juventus still have a long injury list, full-backs Zeki Celik and Andrea Cambiaso have returned to full training and are both in contention to start.

Francisco Conceicao is also back in the fold, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Kamil Grabara, Nico Gonzalez and captain Manuel Locatelli are all unavailable.

Set to start up front, Nick Woltemade finally scored his first Serie A goal against Fiorentina; like strike partner Randal Kolo Muani, he has fared better in this season's Europa League.

After posting three goal involvements from his last two matches, Kolo Muani will hope to continue that form this weekend.

Meanwhile, French wing-back Antoine Hainaut and Nigeria striker Akor Adams are Venezia's joint-top scorers with just two league goals, and the Lagunari have Serie A's lowest shot conversion rate (5.4%).

Either Lion Lauerbach or John Yeboah should partner Adams, the visitors' club-record signing.

Fellow forward Andrea Adorante returned from a layoff during the break, but Marin Sverko and Bartol Franjic are still sidelined.

The pressure is all on Juventus, who have consistently frittered away points with weak defending and wayward finishing.

#1714. FC Twente vs Willem II - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58

Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste

The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.

Twente’s 2-2 draw against Ajax just before the break saw their four-game winning run come to an end, but given they were 2-0 down midway through the second half, securing a share of the spoils resoundingly feels like a point earned rather than two lost.

Just two points behind current leaders PSV Eindhoven, John van den Brom’s side remain firmly in the title race. While they trail Feyenoord, PSV, and Ajax in goals scored, they boast the league's best defence with just 12 goals conceded, and only Heerenveen have kept more clean sheets.

Three weeks after recording their largest-ever win - a 9-0 thrashing of SBV Excelsior - the Tukkers have a chance to lay down another marker against the division’s bottom club. Given rising expectations, a victory here feels almost non-negotiable.

On a personal note, Van den Brom will also want to preserve his impressive record against this weekend’s opposite number; across their previous 11 meetings, the Twente boss has recorded seven wins and four draws.

After winning each of their first home league matches this term, Sunday’s hosts have collected just one point from their last two outings and now seek to avoid going three straight Eredivisie matches in Enschede without a win for the first time since April 2025.

Willem II ended a run of six consecutive league defeats with a 1-1 draw against PEC Zwolle on November 6, but their wait for a first victory continues, as the appointment of Jurgen Streppel has yet to yield the desired turnaround.

Streppel returned for a second spell to replace John Stegeman, who managed just two points from a possible 27 over nine matches. The Zwolle stalemate was only Willem II's third point of the season, at least six fewer than any other team.

Already 12 points worse off than at this stage of their 2024-25 relegation campaign, De Superkruiken face a herculean task to avoid the drop. Upcoming fixtures against Twente and Feyenoord - two of the current top four - over the next three gameweeks only add to their challenge.

A league-high 40 goals conceded means Willem II are frequently punished for their league-low 11 goals scored. Consequently, there must be drastic improvement at one end of the pitch if they are to turn things around.

Facing a team that have scored 14 goals in the final 30 minutes of matches, Sunday’s hosts cannot afford to lose focus in a period in which they have conceded 19 goals, just under half of their season total.

Max Bruns has not featured for Twente since September and remains unavailable, one of two defenders out of contention alongside Stav Lemkin, with the Israeli international suffering a long-term injury just before the start of the season.

Twenty-year-old Filip Erik Thorvaldsen is set to miss a sixth consecutive game for the hosts, who are also still without first-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall.

Wout Weghorst is one of four players tied on nine goals in the Golden Boot race, and the striker will be eager to add to his tally.

Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are Willem II’s two guaranteed absentees for Sunday’s clash, with the latter sidelined since July 2025.

However, French shot-stopper Thomas Didillon could also miss out for the away side, having featured just once since mid-August.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst

Delanghe; Tjoe-A-On, Dekker, Stam, Ter Avest; Twigt, Zarrouk; Van Crooy, Van Aalst, Vilhena; Haen

On paper, Sunday’s fixture appears to be Twente’s easiest game of the season so far, but as has been seen on several occasions, things are rarely that straightforward.

Still, we fully expect the hosts to make light work of their visitors and cruise to all three points at the end of 90 minutes.
