#1659. Pascal Gross: Brighton career assessed after huge contract announcement for “valuable” club legend

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 18:15

Brighton & Hove Albion have announced that Pascal Gross has agreed a new contract with the club until June 2028.

The 35-year-old’s original deal at the Amex Stadium was due to expire at the end of the season, but he has decide to commit his future to the Seagulls by an additional 12 months.

Gross has been rewarded for his talismanic impact back at Brighton since re-joining from boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in January.

The announcement of Gross’s new contract comes ahead of Sunday's Premier League fixture away against Hull City where the midfielder is set to make his 300th club appearance.

"We are really pleased that Pascal has signed a new contract,” head coach Fabian Hurzeler told Brighton’s official website.

"We can talk about his many qualities on the pitch - his goals, assists and football intelligence - but he is also a great leader within the group.

"He connects different generations and different nationalities in our squad. He's so valuable because he helps everyone understand what it takes to be successful."

We are delighted to confirm that Pascal Gross has agreed a new contract with the club! ?

Hurzeler also spoke highly of Gross at his pre-match press conference ahead of their trip to Hull, telling reporters: “He's very adaptive to every personality, and he finds access to every person.

“I think that's something we shouldn't underestimate, and therefore he's so valuable because he gives everyone an understanding of what it needs to be successful.

“No matter if you are 19, 20 years old, no matter if you are 27 or 32, and no matter where you come from, it's all about our standards.

“He's a great standard driver, culture driver, together with Jason (Steele), together with Lewis (Dunk). They are very helpful in driving these things, and therefore I think that's his biggest impact.

#1658. Newcastle a challenge but a good post-Interlull opportunity

Arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home. It’s been a difficult place to visit over the years, and we’ve had some unenjoyable encounters – there particularly during Eddie Howe’s tenure. However, Mikel Arteta more or less has a full squad to choose from, and this version of Newcastle under new manager Matthias Jaissle haven’t been at all convincing so far this season.

In terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break. My gut feeling is that the Dutchman will start today with White penciled in for Borussia Dortmund in midweek. William Saliba is back after another behind closed doors appearance to build his fitness, but for a game that’s likely to be intense and physical, I can’t see anything other than Ezri Konsa alongside Gabriel today. The Frenchman often needs a game or two to get his rhythm back, and while friendlies are useful, they’re not quite the same as competitive minutes. He too is likely to feature in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England. The form of Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard means they’re first picks, and then it’s about how the manager views Bruno Guimaraes for a game like this. Even if Newcastle haven’t been great, the pantomime villain in midfield adds a layer of spice that is inevitable after his summer move. If he wants to keep the crowd quiet, he could choose Myles Lewis-Skelly, but he paid £75m for this player for a good reason, and I think we’ll see the Brazilian from the start.

He was a hugely important player for Newcastle, and while I don’t think his departure was among the most contentious we’ve ever seen, he will be a target for their fans, and perhaps for players who know him – and his temper – very well. You’d hope at 28 he’s mature enough to deal with all that, and I’m sure conversations will have been had about not rising to any bait. Arteta has said more than once recently he wants more from this player, where better to give that than his former club?

As for the front three, I think it will be Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke either side of Kai Havertz. The injury news for Bukayo Saka means he’s going to miss another month, at least, so there’s a big onus on Madueke to continue his recent improved form, but we’ll need him to add end product to the one goal and one assist he’s provided in the league so far. Similarly, Tzolis had a bright-ish start to his Arsenal career, and while the hamstring injury was ill-timed, we need a player who is ostensibly our first choice left winger to start delivering more in terms of assists but especially goals.

Havertz got the winner away to Liverpool, but had frustrating moments at home to Hull. He’s got Viktor Gyokeres on the bench to put some pressure on him, but this front three has some convincing to do and today would be a very good day to produce performances and end product.

Arteta was asked if the atmosphere at St James’ Park isn’t quite what it used to be, because of the way the team has changed and the inconsistent form they’ve suffered so far this campaign. His message was clear:

If that’s the case, it will be even more difficult, because they will be even better prepared, they will have even more necessity to do that, and that’s what we expect. We always expect the best version from the opponent. That’s how we have to prepare for the game, and that’s how we’re going to approach it.

So, there’s no chance he’s letting his team think for a second this might be easier because it’s not the same Newcastle that have caused us problems in recent seasons. Nevertheless, he must have looked at this team and some of the issues they’ve had under their new manager and recognised that this is an opportunity to go there with a settled side of his own in good form and come away with all three points.

It is always a challenge there, but this is a mature Arsenal that should be capable of dealing with a team that has just three wins from thirteen games in all competitions this season. You never take anything for granted, but if we can keep the ball in the early stages, get control, and perhaps even an early goal, the ingredients are there for us to make this a winning start to what is a tricky run of games over the coming weeks. Fingers crossed.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. #1656. Augsburg vs Mainz 05 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:54

Augsburg's WWK Arena will be the backdrop for their clash with Mainz 05 on Sunday in a potentially pivotal clash in the battle against relegation.

The home side are 14th in the Bundesliga table with nine points, whereas their opponents are 12th with 10, and a loss for either could leave them in the bottom three.

Augsburg are only two points above 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the relegation playoff spot, while they are just three points ahead of 17th-placed Schalke 04.

The hosts are winless in their past seven league matches, a period in which they claimed just three points and suffered four defeats.

Head coach Manuel Baum will not be pleased that his team conceded at least two goals in six of those fixtures, though he will highlight that the club netted 13 times in that stretch.

Fuggerstadter have played five contests at WWK Arena in 2026-27, and they have triumphed once, drawn three times and won once at the stadium.

Two of those stalemates came against Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen, while their only defeat at home came against third-placed Freiburg at the end of October.

The visitors come into the clash looking to avoid a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions, and avoid losing a fourth straight Bundesliga game.

Perhaps the saving grace for Mainz is that the rest of the bottom seven play teams currently in the top eight, meaning it is unlikely that they will end the weekend in the relegation zone.

Urs Fischer's side did score four goals in their four losses, but they conceded on 11 occasions, and their latest defeat saw them ship twice when they lost 2-1 against Bayern Munich on November 7.

Mainz's record on the road has been largely positive this term, as while they were beaten 4-1 by Elversberg on October 30, they did emerge as winners in their first three away Bundesliga outings of the campaign.

The club are also unbeaten in their five most recent meetings with Augsburg, claiming victory four times, including when they won 2-0 in February.

Augsburg only have two confirmed absentees, with Han-Noah Massengo and defender Chrislain Matsima ruled out.

Juma Bah, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw and Yannik Keitel could be trusted together in defence, while Robin Fellhauer and Fabian Rieder may start in a double pivot.

Striker Michael Gregoritsch has scored five times in the league this season, and he is certain to lead the line, supported by Anton Kade and Alexis Claude-Maurice.

Though Mainz only have to contend with the absence of centre-back Dominik Kohr, he is not scheduled to return until January because of an ankle injury.

Stefan Posch, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are likely candidates to start in the team's back three, and the trio may be protected by Paul Nebel and Kaishu Sano from midfield.

Dahmen; Bah, Gouweleeuw, Keitel; Wolf, Fellhauer, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Claude-Maurice; Gregoritsch

Zentner; Posch, Gruber, Potulski; Caci, Nebel, Sano, Amiri, Mwene; Tietz, Becker

Neither Augsburg nor Mainz have been particularly strong defensively, so it would be surprising if either kept a clean sheet.

The hosts boast the advantage of playing at WWK Arena, but the visitors have often travelled well, and the two may ultimately have to settle for a point on Sunday.

“We’ll see if the formula can change in January, but on the one hand, Deco says so, on the other, there’s the reality: if Balde doesn’t play as well as he hasn’t been playing between now and January, the idea of ​​Balde leaving could become concrete.

“We told you that he’s currently being offered to Roma, but the Giallorossi haven’t really picked up steam yet. They’ve also offered him to Milan; the player was initially proposed last summer, but without a transfer, nothing happened.

“We’ll see what happens with Alejandro Balde, but he’s a name for the international or possibly Italian market that we need to keep there.”

Considering Sankhoun Diawara is now being considered as a left-back, the situation is certainly not ideal. So, Milan could certainly do worse than signing Balde.

#1654. Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the issue with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager said.

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic."

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively new challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

"It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place."

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret."

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the issue is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's new restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

#1653. Brentford news: Keith Andrews confirms double injury blow ahead of Everton meeting

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 19:13, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:13

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Aaron Hickey and Nathan Collins will be out for a "number of weeks".

Hickey was forced off with a hamstring injury in the first half of Scotland's 4-0 defeat against Switzerland in Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The full-back, who has a history of hamstring problems, is now set for a spell on the sidelines along with Nathan Collins, who missed the Republic of Ireland's 3-0 win over Kosovo with a knee issue.

“No, they won't be available for a number of weeks,” Andrews said when he spoke to reporters ahead of Monday's Premier League meeting with Everton.

“I was actually watching Aaron's game as it happened and I'm just so bitterly disappointed for him.

“He's had such a painful journey on that front with injury, so it's really disappointing for him.

“Similarly with Nathan, he's obviously had a period out with his calf. He's done really well to get back ahead of schedule and played a couple of games.

“These international games came at a really good time for him to get good game time and obviously represent his country, and unfortunately he's hurt his knee. Nathan will be out for a couple of weeks or so.”

Brentford are also without the first-choice striker Igor Thiago, who will serve a three-match ban after being sent off in the 2-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international window.

The Bees are also without the injured duo of Rico Henry and Kaye Furo, while Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo are not ready to return to first-team action despite making progress in their respective recoveries.

In positive news, Andrews has revealed Fabio Carvalho has "every chance" of featuring in Monday's squad after missing the last four games through injury.

Brentford head into the weekend in eighth place in the Premier League table, but they are not in the best of form after winning just one of their last five league games.

#1652. You're Not Nineteenth Forever! Sacked Man United manager Michael Carrick looks relieved to be out of the relegation fight as he watches The Courteeners at gig in London

Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey)

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

#1649. Ajax vs. ADO Den Haag - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how new boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

#1646. New heights and same problems: How Milan stars fared in the November international break

With just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

Whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about…

Christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s quickly reminded everyone of how important he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

It gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

In terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

He played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

It was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

#1645. Coventry vs. Crystal Palace: How Frank Lampard compares to Thomas Frank as relegation warning sent

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.

Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under new head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.

The hosts, meanwhile, are three places and two points better off in the relative safety of 17th spot, having taken nine points from their opening 10 games of their first top-flight season in 25 years.

Two of Coventry's three league triumphs this season have come at the CBS Arena, both against bottom-half rivals in Newcastle United and Sunderland, although Fulham and Hull City have also got the better of them in front of their own fans.

Former Coventry striker Mark Hateley - who scored 27 goals in a century of appearances for the Sky Blues - is fearing a new manager bounce for Palace, but warned his old club that this type of match could dictate their survival chances.

“You always get that bounce from a new manager," Hateley said. "You get it for one, two, three games, and then it starts to wear off. Thomas Frank is a proven tactician who sees things very quickly within a team.

“Palace still have a really decent side with decent players, so I think he'll be in and about it quickly, and you'll see a style of play that he gets from what he sees in that group of players. Whether it lasts all the way through, I don't know, but I think he'll fix Palace into a side that will be OK.

“Coventry are the other side. They've got to survive this year and build for the next two years: survival, survival, survival. Palace will know how to do it; they've got good enough players. But these are the games Coventry should be looking to win. These are the games that keep you in the league.”

Saturday's match will mark the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal Palace since the 2011-12 Championship season, when the Sky Blues lost 2-1 away before holding the Eagles to a 1-1 draw at home.

Coventry earned their most recent victory against Crystal Palace shortly beforehand, prevailing 2-1 in February 2011 thanks to goals from Richard Wood and Marlon King.

Taking data across all competitions from Lampard's Coventry tenure so far and Frank's lengthy spell at Brentford from 2018 to 2025, the statistics somewhat favour the Chelsea legend.

Indeed, Lampard boasts more points per game, more goals scored per match and fewer goals conceded per match, while also winning one trophy in the form of the Championship.

However, those numbers must certainly be taken with a pinch of salt given Frank's substantially longer spell at Brentford, and the Dane's four full seasons in the top flight after winning promotion with the Bees.

Lampard's Coventry have nevertheless shown promising signs after he also succeeded in keeping Everton afloat in the top flight, though, so Saturday's edition of Frank vs. Frank is a challenging one to call.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

#1644. Report: Surprise Liverpool interest set to force quick contract agreement

Surprise interest from Liverpool is set to force a quick contract agreement. The Reds are busy looking for the right player for them.

Liverpool are in the process of weighing up midfield targets as it's increasingly clear that they require a rethink in the position. The plan of simply building around Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai looks to be out of the window already.

And that clearly was the plan. Liverpool handed a bumper new contract to each of them this year only for Andoni Iraola to opt for a midfield pairing of Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister.

It feels like the current situation isn't really tenable - especially after selling Curtis Jones in the summer and not replacing him. It all leaves Liverpool short on numbers and in need of a new direction and we fully expect it'll force them back into the transfer market.

Possibly even in the winter, in fact. Extra midfield balance would significantly increase the chances of Liverpool earning silverware this season.

And that's something which has certain teams scared.

Liverpool look at Ao TanakaTeamTalk claims that Liverpool are one to watch in the running to sign Leeds United's Ao Tanaka. Tanaka's contract expires in 2028 and that has Leeds worried, especially as interest in him grows. Interest that, apparently, does include Liverpool. They're named alongside the likes of Chelsea as wanting Tanaka and potentially making a move in 2027. Leeds, after all, would be forced to sell if they can't agree a new deal. There's no real chance of them letting him go for nothing down the line.

TeamTalk claims that Liverpool are one to watch in the running to sign Leeds United's Ao Tanaka. Tanaka's contract expires in 2028 and that has Leeds worried, especially as interest in him grows.

Interest that, apparently, does include Liverpool. They're named alongside the likes of Chelsea as wanting Tanaka and potentially making a move in 2027.

Leeds, after all, would be forced to sell if they can't agree a new deal. There's no real chance of them letting him go for nothing down the line.

Though, we'd be genuinely shocked if Liverpool was his ultimate destination. The Red part of it, anyway. Tanaka is now 28 and not really of the kind of quality that the Reds would ignore his age to get a deal done.

There's no long-term investment here, in other words, and the short-term wouldn't be good enough to justify a fee. Really the only players in that age bracket that Liverpool have signed within the past 10 years are Wataru Endo and Thiago.

Both were special cases. Endo was needed because the squad lacked a specialist defensive midfielder at a time when Liverpool really needed one. And Thiago was needed because he was Thiago.

Tanaka ticks neither box. If he were completely free, things would change but there's no chance Liverpool are considering potential free transfers in 2028. Instead, we imagine this is actually agents driving up interest to get Leeds moving on a contract.

#1643. Racing de Santander vs Real Sociedad - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 20:16, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:18

Both Racing de Santander and Real Sociedad will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in Spain's top flight when they lock horns on Sunday afternoon.

Real Sociedad lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 49 wins to 34, while the Basque outfit have triumphed in the last three meetings.

Racing have a record of four wins, two draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 14 points leaving them in 10th spot in the La Liga table.

Jose Alberto's side entered the November international break off the back of a 2-1 victory over Malaga, and they have actually won three of their last four games in all competitions.

The Green and Whites are the reigning Segunda Division champions, securing a return to this level courtesy of their excellent second-tier campaign in 2025-26, and their main aim for this season will be to consolidate back in the top flight.

Racing have not managed to overcome Real Sociedad since March 2011, while they have just one victory over the Basque side since January 2007.

The Green and Whites have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 11 points from their six matches in front of their own supporters.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, boast a record of seven wins, one draw and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 22 points leaving them fifth in the table.

The Basque outfit are only four points off fourth-placed Real Betis, and an excellent run of form in Spain's top flight has seen them win five of their last six matches.

La Real are also playing in the Europa League this season, picking up five points from their four matches to sit down in 20th position in the league stage.

Real Sociedad's last league match ended in a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano before the November international break, and they will have their eyes on another three points here before heading to England next week to tackle Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

Racing de Santander form (all competitions):

Racing need to make late checks on Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin, but the hosts are otherwise in strong shape for their clash with Real Sociedad.

Yassir Zabiri has been in impressive form this season, scoring nine goals in 12 appearances, and the number 21 will continue through the middle for the hosts.

There is also expected to be a spot in the side for Ivan Martin.

As for Real Sociedad, Alvaro Odriozola remains unavailable for selection due to a knee injury, while Ander Barrenetxea is a major doubt due to a hamstring injury.

Mikel Oyarzabal missed the team's final match ahead of the November international break through illness, but the attacker has since returned for Spain, and it is possible that he could start in a wide area on Sunday due to the form of Orri Oskarsson.

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure…

#1641. Juan Mata retires aged 38: Premier League legend calls time on glittering career as Manchester United pay tribute to former star

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq

Juan Mata has announced his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata)

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'

Chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

Liverpool's players are thrilled. Two ridiculously good players have finally joined up with them - and now the squad looks better for it.

Liverpool hope to improve in a few ways this season. One is by getting used to Andoni Iraola's plans and gelling as a unit. Another is by the improvement of developing players, such as Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha.

#1639. Sparta Rotterdam vs AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58

A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.

The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.

AZ Alkmaar started the season with six wins and a draw from their opening seven Eredivisie matches, looking like the team to beat, but a 2-0 defeat to Feyenoord after the September break sparked a four-game winless run (D1, L3).

In arguably the game of the season so far, Leeroy Echteld’s men scored three times in the final 30 minutes of their most recent clash against Groningen to secure a 4-3 victory and keep themselves within three points of PSV Eindhoven at the top of the Eredivisie table.

De Kaasboeren have failed to win any of their league matches immediately preceding a Europa League group-stage fixture so far, and with a trip to Sparta Prague to follow this weekend, they will be eager to buck that trend of faltering domestically before continental duties.

AZ won both league meetings with Sparta last season, making it four wins from the last six encounters (D1, L1). Sunday’s visitors are also unbeaten in their last six trips to Het Kasteel, averaging two goals per game in that stretch.

However, AZ have struggled away from home recently, collecting just one point from the last nine available on their travels, which came in a 2-2 draw at Cambuur courtesy of a Mexx Merdink penalty seven minutes from time.

While not their heaviest, Sparta’s 3-1 defeat to newly-promoted ADO Den Haag was arguably their most disappointing loss of the 2026-27 season so far, especially given the momentum they carried into the clash after a thrilling 3-2 triumph over Groningen.

Rogier Meijer has now lost more than half of his 13 matches since taking charge in July, and pressure is beginning to mount on the 45-year-old.

Nevertheless, his experience at this level - having recently surpassed 200 matches as a manager in Dutch football - suggests he will be given time to turn things around.

Starting this weekend’s clash just two points clear of the drop zone, De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren risk ending matchday 13 inside the relegation places - a significant fall from grace for a side tipped to compete for Europe at the start of the campaign.

Only Utrecht and Willem II have conceded more goals than Sparta’s 29, and they are also one of five teams without a clean sheet, leaving little mystery about their biggest shortcoming this season.

Averaging 1.8 goals per game so far, Sunday’s hosts have fared reasonably well in attack, but an overreliance on Milan Zonneveld, who has been directly involved in nine of their 21 goals, can sometimes prove detrimental.

Sparta Rotterdam form (all competitions):

Goalkeeper Michael Brouwer is Sparta’s only injury concern for Sunday’s clash after he was forced off late in the defeat to ADO Den Haag.

Filip Bednarek replaced Brouwer off the bench last time out and is ready to deputise in goal again if required.

Lushendry Martes will need to keep his discipline in check, having already collected four yellow cards this season, as one more would trigger a one-match suspension.

Jizz Hornkamp has made just three appearances this season and remains unavailable for AZ, as do fellow Dutchmen Stije Resink and Jeroen Zoet, who are both yet to feature in 2026-27.

Lewis Schouten’s involvement this weekend is currently in doubt after he was absent from the win over Groningen.

Twenty-three-year-old Mexx Meerdink has six goals and an assist in his last seven club matches and will be expected to deliver once again.

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:

Bednarek; Martes, Young, Verschuren, Martins Indi, Kuipers; Van Bergen, Quintero, Hatenboer, Babadi; Zonneveld

De Busser; Chavez, Hoedt, Goes, Dijkstra; Koopmeiners, Kwakman; Daal, Byskov, Oufkir; Meerdink

While Sparta’s defensive issues need no introduction, AZ have also struggled at the back recently, so a clean sheet for either side seems unlikely.

That said, Echteld’s men are strong favourites to get the job done, and we expect them to do so with relative ease.

#1636. Nico Paz compared to Messi and Maradona amid Real Madrid return rumours

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01

Real Madrid's reported plans to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, Madrid have decided to exercise the clause, which can only be triggered during the summer 2027 transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 14 club appearances this season, establishing himself as one of the most influential attacking midfielders in Italian football.

However, Veron's latest assessment of Paz offers more than an extraordinary comparison with two of Argentina's greatest players.

The former Argentina international has also emphasised the importance of regular football in developing young talents, a consideration that could become significant if Paz returns to a Madrid squad already containing Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler.

Speaking in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Veron reserved exceptional praise for Paz after the midfielder continued his impressive international development.

"Nico Paz has incredible talent. He is destined for great things," the former Manchester United midfielder said. "The future belongs to him if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing."

Veron then made a particularly striking comparison. "At 22, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do certain things like that."

The 51-year-old was careful not to suggest that Paz was guaranteed to reach the extraordinary heights achieved by either legend. "I don't mean that he will reach those levels, but he has the qualities to attempt it," Veron explained.

What particularly impresses the former Chelsea midfielder is the confidence Paz displays when receiving possession under pressure.

Veron highlighted the youngster's ability to dictate the rhythm of attacks, move into dangerous positions and retain the trust of his teammates even when closely marked.

Rather than describing him solely as an individual talent, he identified Paz as the player around whom Como organise much of their attacking football.

"Nico is a leader in the way he manages moves. He is the focal point of the game," Veron added.

Those qualities have become increasingly apparent under Fabregas, whose possession-based approach has allowed the Argentine to develop into a central figure.

Paz has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He recently scored twice for Argentina against Costa Rica, further strengthening his credentials as one of the country's leading young talents following Messi's international retirement.

His performances have inevitably increased speculation surrounding his next move, with Madrid retaining a significant advantage over other potential suitors.

Paz left Madrid for Como in the summer of 2024, having made only eight senior appearances for the Spanish giants.

His move to Italy initially offered an opportunity to gain regular first-team experience, but the relationship between the two clubs has since become more complicated.

During the summer of 2026, Como reportedly paid an additional €60m to acquire full ownership of the player, while Madrid retained a final buy-back option worth €80m.

That clause is valid for the summer of 2027, meaning Madrid have a limited opportunity to bring their former academy player back on preferential terms.

COPE now reports that the Spanish giants intend to exercise that option, although the deal has not been officially completed.

As previously reported by Sports Mole, Madrid face an important decision over Paz's future, particularly because of the attacking competition awaiting him at the Bernabeu.

Bellingham has established himself as a key figure in Madrid's midfield, while Guler has also become increasingly influential under Jose Mourinho.

The club possesses several other attacking options, including Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande. Consequently, there is no guarantee that Paz would enjoy the same importance in Madrid's starting XI that he currently possesses at Como.

Veron's comments about another young Argentine, Franco Mastantuono, offer an interesting perspective on that challenge.

Discussing the youngster's development during his loan spell at Fiorentina, Veron argued that consistent opportunities were essential for establishing himself at the highest level.

"Nico Paz became a leader at Como by playing," he explained. "I have never known a player who became a team leader by sitting on the bench."

Veron was discussing the benefits of regular football rather than explicitly warning Paz against returning to Madrid. Nevertheless, his observations underline an important consideration for the Spanish club as it weighs up the midfielder's future.

Paz reportedly chose to remain at Como last summer because he wanted to continue developing through regular appearances, and his decision has been rewarded by an outstanding start to the new campaign.

Manchester United have also been linked with the Argentina international, although Madrid's contractual advantage places the Spanish giants in a stronger position.

For Los Blancos, securing a player whose value has risen considerably could represent an attractive investment. For Paz, the sporting challenge would be to turn the promise recognised by Veron into an influential role at a club where competition for attacking positions is already fierce.
